name: Michael Johnson
opening_statement: I've been having this chest tightness on and off for the past 3 days, and it's getting worse. This morning it woke me up from sleep.
emotional_baseline: Anxious and worried, speaks with slightly labored breathing, clutching chest intermittently

symptoms.name: Chest pain/tightness
symptoms.character: Heavy pressure, like a weight on chest
symptoms.location: Central chest, radiating to left arm and jaw
symptoms.onset: Gradual over 3 days, acute worsening this morning
symptoms.timing: Intermittent, episodes lasting 10-20 minutes, occurring at rest
symptoms.relieving_factors: Rest provides minimal relief, GTN previously effective but not today

rag_citation.guideline: Typical anginal symptoms include central chest pressure radiating to arm/jaw, associated with diaphoresis and dyspnea. Rest pain or crescendo pattern indicates high-risk ACS.
Dyspnea at rest or minimal exertion with orthopnea suggests acute LV dysfunction, common complication of ACS.
Diaphoresis is a key autonomic symptom in ACS, particularly with NSTEMI, indicating significant cardiac ischemia.
Nausea/vomiting can occur with ACS, particularly inferior wall MI, due to vagal stimulation.

family_history: Father had MI at age 68, died at 74 from CVA. Mother has hypertension and diabetes, alive at 89. One brother with hypertension.

social_history.alcohol: Social drinker, 2-3 standard drinks per week
social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife in own home, independent ADLs
social_history.exercise: Previously walked 30 minutes daily, reduced to 10 minutes over past week due to symptoms
social_history.diet: Generally healthy, trying to follow diabetic diet
social_history.social_support: Strong - wife present, two adult children nearby

examination_findings.general_appearance: Alert, anxious, mild diaphoresis, appears uncomfortable

cardiovascular.inspection: No visible JVP elevation at 45°, no peripheral edema
cardiovascular.palpation: Apex beat displaced laterally (6th ICS, AAL), normal character
cardiovascular.auscultation: Dual heart sounds, soft S4 gallop, no murmurs/rubs. Peripheral pulses present and equal bilaterally.

respiratory.inspection: Mild tachypnea, no cyanosis, no accessory muscle use
respiratory.auscultation: Bibasal fine inspiratory crackles, no wheezes

examination_findings.abdominal: Soft, non-tender, no organomegaly, bowel sounds normal
examination_findings.neurological: Alert and oriented x3, no focal deficits, equal pupils reactive to light

ecg.findings: Sinus rhythm 92 bpm. ST depression 1.5mm in leads V4-V6, I, aVL. T-wave inversion in leads V5-V6. No Q waves. No LBBB.
ecg.comparison: Previous ECG 6 months ago showed LVH strain pattern only

troponin.interpretation: Positive for myocardial infarction, dynamic rise confirms NSTEMI

investigations.ue: Na 139, K 4.1, Cr 98, eGFR 68 mL/min/1.73m² (CKD stage 2)
investigations.cxr: Mild cardiomegaly (CTR 0.54), early interstitial edema, no consolidation
investigations.bedside_echo_if_available: Moderate LV systolic dysfunction (EF ~40%), regional wall motion abnormality (lateral wall hypokinesis), no pericardial effusion

expected_diagnosis: NSTEMI (Non-ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction) - High Risk

actions: Oxygen if SpO2 <94% (currently 94%, monitor closely)
MONA-B: Morphine 2.5-5mg IV for pain, Oxygen PRN, Nitrates (GTN infusion 10-200 mcg/min), Aspirin 300mg loading (already on 100mg daily), Beta-blocker (metoprolol 25-50mg PO if no contraindications)
Dual antiplatelet: Aspirin 300mg loading PLUS Ticagrelor 180mg loading dose (or Clopidogrel 600mg if ticagrelor contraindicated)
Anticoagulation: Enoxaparin 1mg/kg SC BD or fondaparinux 2.5mg SC daily (consider UFH if early angiography planned)
Statin: Atorvastatin 80mg nocte (high-intensity)
Continuous cardiac monitoring
IV access x2, serial troponins
Urgent cardiology consult for risk stratification (GRACE score calculation)

rag_citation.guideline: NSTEMI management includes immediate antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), anticoagulation, and early invasive strategy for high-risk patients. GRACE score >140 indicates high risk requiring angiography within 24-72 hours.

actions: Coronary angiography ± PCI within 24-72 hours (high-risk NSTEMI: dynamic ST changes, elevated troponin, GRACE score likely >140)
Continue DAPT, anticoagulation until angiography
Optimize medical therapy pre-procedure

rag_citation.guideline: High-risk NSTEMI (ongoing ischemia, dynamic ECG changes, elevated troponin) benefits from early invasive strategy within 24-72 hours.

actions: Dual antiplatelet therapy: Aspirin 100mg daily + Ticagrelor 90mg BD for 12 months
High-intensity statin: Atorvastatin 80mg nocte (target LDL <1.8 mmol/L)
ACE inhibitor: Continue perindopril, uptitrate if tolerated (target dose 8-10mg)
Beta-blocker: Add metoprolol 25mg BD, uptitrate to 50-100mg BD (target HR 50-60)
Optimize glycemic control: Review diabetes management, consider addition of SGLT2i or GLP-1 RA for cardioprotection
Cardiac rehabilitation referral
Lifestyle modification: smoking cessation (maintained), diet, exercise program
MBS item 721 (GP Management Plan) for chronic disease management

rag_citation.guideline: Post-ACS patients require comprehensive secondary prevention: DAPT, high-intensity statin, ACE-I/ARB, beta-blocker, and cardiac rehabilitation to reduce recurrent events.

actions: Serial troponins (0h, 3h, 6h to assess for ongoing myocardial injury)
Daily ECGs until stable
Echocardiography for LV function assessment (EF, regional wall motion)
Monitor for complications: cardiogenic shock, arrhythmias, mechanical complications
Post-discharge: Cardiology follow-up in 2-4 weeks, repeat echo in 6-8 weeks

critical_errors.error: Failure to administer dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin + P2Y12 inhibitor) within 24 hours
critical_errors.consequence: Increased risk of recurrent MI, stent thrombosis if PCI performed

critical_errors.error: Discharging patient without cardiology consult or plan for angiography
critical_errors.consequence: High-risk NSTEMI requires early invasive strategy; delayed/missed intervention increases mortality

critical_errors.error: Administering beta-blocker without checking for contraindications (acute HF, bradycardia, hypotension)
critical_errors.consequence: May precipitate cardiogenic shock if LV dysfunction severe

critical_errors.error: Failure to start anticoagulation (LMWH/fondaparinux) in addition to antiplatelets
critical_errors.consequence: Incomplete ACS management, increased thrombus propagation risk

critical_errors.error: Not addressing suboptimal LDL level (2.8 mmol/L) by increasing statin to high-intensity
critical_errors.consequence: Missed opportunity for secondary prevention, target LDL <1.8 mmol/L post-ACS

critical_errors.error: Failure to counsel on cardiac rehabilitation or arrange MBS chronic disease management plan
critical_errors.consequence: Reduced long-term adherence, missed structured support for lifestyle modification

fracp_reviews.credentials: Interventional Cardiologist, Royal Melbourne Hospital; 18 years post-fellowship experience
fracp_reviews.comments: Excellent high-risk NSTEMI case with realistic clinical presentation. ECG findings (lateral ST depression, dynamic changes) accurately reflect ischemia pattern. Management pathway aligns with current Australian guidelines (eTG, NHFA/CSANZ). Good emphasis on GRACE score risk stratification and early invasive strategy. The critical error of discharging without cardiology consult is appropriate - this is a true 'never event' in ACS management. Medication dosing (ticagrelor 180mg load, atorvastatin 80mg) reflects contemporary evidence. Minor suggestion: could add note about radial vs femoral access preference for angiography (radial preferred for bleeding risk reduction).

fracp_reviews.credentials: Director of General Medicine, Austin Health; AMC Clinical Examiner since 2018
fracp_reviews.comments: Well-calibrated Medium difficulty case - appropriate for intermediate AMC candidates. The combination of diabetes, hypertension, and CKD stage 2 reflects real-world complexity without overwhelming the scenario. Social history is comprehensive and relevant (ex-smoker, exercise tolerance decline). Comorbidity count (4 conditions) matches Medium difficulty criteria. The SOCRATES symptom structure for chest pain is complete and typical for ACS. One teaching point: the S4 gallop on examination is a subtle sign of LV stiffness/diastolic dysfunction - good clinical realism. Learning objectives cover key AMC domains: risk stratification, antiplatelet therapy, secondary prevention. FRACP-equivalent content confirmed.

learning_objectives: Differentiate NSTEMI from STEMI using clinical presentation, ECG patterns, and troponin kinetics. Understand that NSTEMI may have ST depression or T-wave changes (not ST elevation) but still requires urgent intervention.

Apply GRACE score for risk stratification in ACS: High-risk features include age >70, elevated troponin, dynamic ECG changes, heart failure signs. High-risk NSTEMI (GRACE >140) warrants early invasive strategy (angiography within 24-72h).

Master dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT): Aspirin 300mg load then 100mg daily + Ticagrelor 180mg load then 90mg BD for 12 months post-ACS. Understand P2Y12 inhibitor options (ticagrelor preferred over clopidogrel for ACS unless contraindications).
Recognize high-risk ECG patterns in ACS: ST depression ≥1mm in multiple leads, dynamic changes, new T-wave inversion. Lateral changes (V4-V6, I, aVL) suggest LAD or circumflex territory ischemia.

Implement comprehensive secondary prevention post-MI: High-intensity statin (atorvastatin 80mg, target LDL <1.8), ACE-I, beta-blocker, cardiac rehab, lifestyle modification. Understand MBS items (721 GP Management Plan) for chronic disease support.

Identify contraindications to beta-blockers in ACS: Acute decompensated heart failure (pulmonary edema, cardiogenic shock), bradycardia <50 bpm, hypotension <100 mmHg systolic, severe asthma/COPD. Check LV function before initiating.

Recognize early heart failure signs in ACS: Bibasal crackles, S4 gallop, mild JVP elevation, orthopnea. Acute LV dysfunction common with NSTEMI - requires careful beta-blocker/ACE-I titration and diuretics if fluid overload.

Apply Australian PBS restrictions for post-ACS medications: DAPT (ticagrelor Authority script for ACS indication), high-intensity statins (streamlined Authority), ACE-I (General Schedule). Counsel on medication costs and adherence.
